rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, plus minerals, enzymes and water — are the chemical basis of life. Monomers join into polymers by condensation (water out) and are split by hydrolysis (water in). Carbohydrates (Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ) supply quick energy and structure; proteins (amino acids + peptide bonds, four structural levels) do the cell's work; lipids (water-insoluble, 9 kcal/g) store…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
General formula of carbohydrates: $C_x(H_2O)_y$ (e.g. glucose $C_6H_{12}O_6$).
Peptide bonds in a polypeptide of $n$ amino acids = $n-1$; water lost = $n-1$.
Condensation: monomer–OH + HO–monomer → polymer + $H_2O$; hydrolysis is the reverse.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Lipid vs carbohydrate as "polymer":** carbohydrates, proteins and nucleic acids are true polymers of repeated monomers; triglycerides are NOT — glycerol and fatty acids are different molecules, not repeated units. NEB loves this trap.  ·  **Nucleoside vs nucleotide:** nucleoside = sugar + base only; nucleotide = sugar + base + phosphate. Only the nucleotide is the true monomer of nucleic acids.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The 2024 NEB paper asked biomolecule classes, nucleotide structure, Watson–Crick features, enzyme properties, carbohydrate classification and fatty-acid differences — this single topic supplied ~18 marks. Treat it as the highest-yield unit of Botany.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆)** — hexose monosaccharide; universal respiratory fuel; blood sugar.  ·  **Sucrose** — non-reducing disaccharide (glucose + fructose); the transport sugar of plant phloem — non-reducing so it does not react en route.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Condensation/hydrolysis cycle** — the universal build-and-break chemistry of every biomolecule.  ·  **Structure determines function** — protein shape (sickle-cell), α vs β glycosidic bonds (starch vs cellulose), amphipathic lipid shape (membrane bilayer).  ·  **Complementary base pairing** — the physical basis of heredity, replication and Chargaff's rule.  ·  **Activation energy lowering** — the single correct explanation of enzyme catalysis.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: **Biomolecules** = carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids + minerals, enzymes, water; built from C, H, O, N, P, S.  ·  Monomer → polymer by **condensation** (water out); polymer → monomer by **hydrolysis** (water in).  ·  Carbohydrates: Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ; mono/di/oligo/poly; glucose = universal fuel; starch/glycogen store, cellulose/chitin structure.  ·  α-bonds (starch) digestible; β-bonds (cellulose) not — humans lack cellulase.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Water is 70–90% of a living cell; protein is ~50% of dry weight.  ·  Energy values: carbohydrate 4 kcal/g, protein 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Why is water called the universal solvent? **Answer.** Because water molecules are **polar** (δ⁺ H, δ⁻ O) and form **hydrogen bonds and hydration shells** around ions and polar molecules, pulling them into solution — water dissolves more substances than any other liquid.…  ·  **Short answer (2m):** What are coenzymes? Give one example. **Answer.** **Small organic, non-protein cofactors** — often **vitamin derivatives** — that some apoenzymes require for activity; they frequently act as transient carriers of atoms or electrons in the reaction.…  ·  **Long answer (5m):** Describe the classification of carbohydrates with examples and state their functions. **Answer.** **Definition:** carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones with the general formula **Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ** — literally “hydrated carbon”.…

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Application favourite: why sucrose (non-reducing) is the transport sugar; why the camel's hump is fat; why ice floats and ponds freeze from the top.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: **Cellulose** — β-1,4 glucose polymer; plant cell wall; human roughage (we lack cellulase; ruminants digest it via symbiotic microbes).  ·  **Chitin** — N-acetylglucosamine polymer; fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Energy density hierarchy** — fat (9) > protein = carbohydrate (4) kcal/g, because lipids are more reduced (less oxygen per carbon).  ·  Energy values: carbohydrate 4 kcal/g; protein 4 kcal/g; lipid 9 kcal/g.  ·  Proteins: 20 amino acids, peptide bond −CO−NH−, 4 structural levels, structure determines function.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Conjugated protein = protein + prosthetic group (haemoglobin = haem + globin).  ·  Lipids: water-insoluble, organic-solvent-soluble; 9 kcal/g; phospholipids are amphipathic → bilayer membranes.  ·  Saturated fats: single bonds, solid, animal; unsaturated: C=C, liquid oils, plant.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nucleotide = pentose + base + phosphate; DNA: deoxyribose + A,T,G,C, double helix; RNA: ribose + A,U,G,C, single strand.  ·  A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds); Chargaff: %A=%T, %G=%C.  ·  Enzymes: protein catalysts; lower activation energy; apoenzyme + cofactor = holoenzyme; six IUB classes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Water: 70–90% of cell; polar, high specific heat, max density at 4 °C, universal solvent, reactant in hydrolysis/photosynthesis.  ·  **Denaturation vs digestion:** denaturation (heat, pH) destroys 3-D shape but leaves peptide bonds intact; hydrolysis (digestion) actually breaks peptide bonds into amino acids.  ·  **Starch vs glycogen vs cellulose:** all are glucose polymers, but starch (plants, α-1,4/1,6), glycogen (animals, more highly branched), cellulose (β-1,4, indigestible). Same monomer, different bonds = different biology.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Competitive vs non-competitive inhibition:** competitive inhibitors bind the active site and can be overcome by more substrate; non-competitive inhibitors bind an allosteric site and cannot.  ·  **Enzyme vs hormone:** enzymes are catalysts (not consumed, act locally on substrates); hormones are chemical messengers (consumed after action, transported by blood to distant targets).  ·  **DNA "contains protein":** DNA is pure nucleic acid; chromosomes contain DNA + histone protein. DNA itself has no protein.
